definition: A coating of white, feathery ice crystals formed when freezing fog or supercooled droplets settle on a surface; also, more broadly, hoarfrost.
etymology: Rime comes from Old English hrīm, “frost,” kin to Old Norse hrím. Over centuries, English let the initial h fall away, leaving the spare, cold-sounding rime.
usage: By late October, the hedges may wear a rime before sunrise, every thorn briefly silvered.
